A.explanation: $\text{J C}^{-1}$ is joule per coulomb, which is the volt for potential difference, not a rate of energy transfer.

B.explanation: $\text{J m}^{-1}$ is joule per metre, which simplifies to the newton for force from $W = Fs$, not power.

C.explanation: $\text{J N}^{-1}$ is joule per newton, which simplifies to metre for distance, not power.

D.explanation: $\text{J s}^{-1}$ is joule per second, which matches $P = W/t$ and is the watt for power.

hints: Recall what power measures: energy $W$ in joules transferred per time $t$ in seconds, so look for joule divided by second.
Write the defining relation $P = W/t$ and check what unit you get when $W$ is in $\text{J}$ and $t$ is in $\text{s}$.
Compare the denominators in the four options - $\text{C}$, $\text{m}$, $\text{N}$ and $\text{s}$ - and ask which denominator gives energy per unit time.
walkthrough: Identify the given quantity: power is defined as the rate of work done or energy transferred.
State the governing rule: $P = W/t$, where work $W$ is measured in joules ($\text{J}$) and time $t$ in seconds ($\text{s}$).
Combine the units: the unit of $P$ must therefore be joule divided by second, $\text{J}/\text{s} = \text{J s}^{-1}$, also called the watt.
Check the other combinations: $\text{J C}^{-1}$ is $\text{V}$, $\text{J m}^{-1}$ is $\text{N}$, and $\text{J N}^{-1}$ is $\text{m}$, so none is a rate of energy.
Only $\text{J s}^{-1}$ has the form energy per time. This is option D.
